questions.q: Where is the Query Plan tool enabled in the Developer Console?
options: It is enabled by default and needs no setup
Help → Preferences, by selecting Enable Query Plan
Setup → Query Settings
It can only be enabled through the REST API
questions.explain: The Query Plan tool is off by default; it's turned on from the Developer Console's Help → Preferences menu.

questions.q: What does a query's 'cost' figure in the Query Plan tool roughly indicate?
options: The number of fields included in the SELECT list
The exact number of seconds the query will take to run
The number of governor-limit SOQL queries the statement counts as
A cost at or below 1 generally indicates the query is selective; above 1 suggests it isn't
questions.explain: Cost compares the query against the selectivity threshold — a cost of 1 or below generally signals a selective query, above 1 signals it likely falls back to a broader scan.

questions.q: What does a leading operation type of TableScan mean?
options: The optimizer intends to scan the table broadly rather than use an index
The query will definitely fail at runtime
The query is guaranteed to be the fastest possible plan
The query only works on custom objects
questions.explain: TableScan means the optimizer's plan involves a broad scan rather than an index lookup — generally undesirable for a query expected to run efficiently at scale.

questions.q: When the Query Plan tool shows multiple candidate plans for one query, which plan does Salesforce actually use?
options: The plan with the highest cardinality
Always the first plan listed, regardless of cost
Whichever plan has the minimum cost
The developer must manually select which plan to use
questions.explain: Salesforce automatically executes the plan with the minimum cost; the tool's job is to show you what the optimizer decided and why, not to let you pick.

questions.q: How can you get the same query-plan information outside the Developer Console, e.g. from a script or CI pipeline?
options: There is no way to access Query Plan data outside the Developer Console
Using the REST API's query resource with the explain parameter
By running the query in SOSL instead of SOQL
By adding ORDER BY to the query
questions.explain: The REST API's explain parameter on the query resource returns the same plan options, cost, cardinality, and leading operation type data.
